brief.topic: The Rods That Quietly Copy a Shape

s01: One point follows a small outline.
Another point draws the same shape, twice as large.
The rods between them are doing the copying.
Pause and look at the fixed pivot.
Two sides form a small triangle, and two longer sides form a larger one.
Their directions match because opposite sides of the hinged parallelogram stay parallel.
The long side from the pivot is twice its matching short side.
The triangles therefore have the same shape at a scale of two.
The copying point stays twice as far from the pivot as the tracing point.
Every part of the small outline gets the same enlargement.
Lengths double, while angles keep their size.
This drawing tool is a pantograph.
Its ideal rods keep fixed lengths, and its joints turn freely.
Swap which point traces and which point draws.
The same arrangement can make a copy half as large.

scenes.narration:
One point follows a small outline. Another point draws the same shape, twice as large. The rods between them are doing the copying.

Pause and look at the fixed pivot. Two sides form a small triangle, and two longer sides form a larger one. Their directions match because opposite sides of the hinged parallelogram stay parallel.

The long side from the pivot is twice its matching short side. The triangles therefore have the same shape at a scale of two. The copying point stays twice as far from the pivot as the tracing point.

Let the points move again. Every part of the small outline gets the same enlargement. Lengths double, while angles keep their size.

This drawing tool is a pantograph. Its ideal rods keep fixed lengths, and its joints turn freely. Swap which point traces and which point draws. The same arrangement can make a copy half as large.
